sn2.9:1.2: Then at that time the Moon god was seized by the asura lord Rāhu.
sn2.9:1.3: Then the Moon god, recollecting the Fortunate One, on that occasion recited this verse:
sn2.9:2.1: “Reverence to you, Buddha-hero, you who are free in every way!
sn2.9:2.3: I am being obstructed therefore please be a refuge to me.”
sn2.9:3.1: Then, with reference to the Moon god, the Fortunate One addressed the asura lord Rāhu with a verse:
sn2.9:4.1: “To the Realised One, the Worthy One, the Moon has gone for refuge,
sn2.9:4.3: you must release the Moon, Rāhu! (For) the Buddhas pity the world.”
sn2.9:5.1: Then the asura lord Rāhu, having released the Moon god, hurriedly approached the asura lord Vepacitti, and after approaching, anxious, and horrified, he stood on one side.
sn2.9:5.2: While he was standing on one side the asura lord Vepacitti recited this verse to the asura lord Rāhu:
sn2.9:6.1: “Why did you so hurriedly release the Moon god, Rāhu?
sn2.9:6.3: After coming (here) why do you stand (there) like someone anxious and frightened?”
sn2.9:7.2: while living I will have no happiness,
sn2.9:7.3: - I am one to whom the Buddha has chanted a verse - if I do not release the Moon.”
